calls.head: The Jets’ defense joins the attack; the Red Wings’ stays home
calls.body: The Jets are one of the league’s best for shots from defensemen, at the active D end; the Red Wings are around the middle of the league, at the forward-led end. Expect that gap to show.
calls.call: The Jets’ defensemen take a bigger share of the team’s shot attempts than the Red Wings’.
calls.cite: Style fingerprint · this season blended with last · 1 and 1 games this season
calls.happened: On share of 5-on-5 shot attempts taken by defensemen, Winnipeg had 33% and Detroit 30%. Coming in, Winnipeg was at 37% and Detroit at 34%.

calls.head: Sheltered against exposed
calls.body: On preventing dangerous shots, Winnipeg is around the middle of the league and Detroit is one of the league’s worst. That’s about as far apart as two teams get.
calls.call: The Jets prevent dangerous shots better than the Red Wings do.
calls.cite: Style fingerprint · this season blended with last · 1 and 1 games this season
calls.happened: On how dangerous the average shot allowed was, Winnipeg had 6.9% a shot and Detroit 5.7% a shot. Coming in, Winnipeg was at 6.3% a shot and Detroit at 6.5% a shot.
calls.usual: WPG 6.3% a shot · DET 6.5% a shot

DET.head: We had this close to even (47% for Detroit), and it went Winnipeg’s way.

WPG.head: We had this close to even (53% for Winnipeg), and Winnipeg came through.

surprises.head: Winnipeg won against the run of play
surprises.body: Played out 100 times with these chances, Detroit wins 76. Winnipeg won anyway.

story.head: Skinner steals one in Detroit
paras: Cole Perfetti opened the scoring midway through the first. Kyle Connor added two power-play goals.
The Red Wings had the better of the play. Replay the chances a hundred times and the Red Wings win about four in five. Stuart Skinner made the difference in net, stopping 34 of 36.

items.text: One of the preview’s two calls held.
